scan: V ⊂ V^⊥ .  (the ⊥ written by hand after the second V)
note: The printed inclusion is reversed. By the diagram (2.5.4) on folio 341, rank V/W = 2α and rank V^⊥/W = 2λ, so V ⊂ V^⊥ means α = 0, not semi-stability: with good reduction V = U and V^⊥ = 0, and the printed (ii) fails. The proof on this page ends 'V^⊥ ⊂ U^I=V, ce qui est (ii)', and (ii) ⟺ (iii) through W = V∩V^⊥ holds only for V^⊥ ⊂ V. A slip of the original (the author's, or of the hand-inserted ⊥ signs), not a typewriter error; it goes with the misprinted (2.5.5) on folio 341. Apply together with the next entry and with the (2.5.5) correction. The TeX keeps the printed reading. 'corrected' replaces the 'tex' substring.
